whatItDoes: Computes the Return on Investment (ROI) for an investment. Enter the amount invested and the final value to get the net profit, the simple ROI percentage, and the annualized ROI when a holding period is given.
whyItExists: Fundamentally, has an investment made money after accounting for the full outlay? ROI expresses that answer as a plain percentage and annualizes it, so returns on different sizes of money and timeframes become easy to compare.
whoShouldUse: Self-directed investors, small-business owners, and startups measuring the effectiveness of capital spent.
useCases: Measure the profit generated by an investment
Compare returns across assets of different sizes
See the annualized return when you hold a position for several years
Evaluate business or marketing spend effectiveness
instructions: Enter the total amount you invested
Enter the current or final value of the investment
Optionally enter the holding period in years
Read the net profit, ROI percentage, and annualized ROI
bestPractices: Include every cost that affects the out-of-pocket investment
Prefer annualized ROI for multi-year comparisons
Use realistic, all-in ending values between fees
Track your own benchmarks to evaluate a strategy over time
commonMistakes: Comparing simple ROI of different holding periods
Forgetting brokerage fees that reduce the net return
Entering a period of zero while expecting an annualized figure
Treating ROI as guaranteed future performance
faq: What is ROI? — It is profit divided by the total outlay, expressed as a percent.
What is annualized ROI? — The ROI scaled to a per-year rate so periods can be compared.
Can ROI be negative? — Yes: when final value is below the amount invested.
Is my data sent to servers? — Never, it is computed locally in your browser.
features: Annualized ROI with optional holding period
